title: Is Safer Better? The Impact of Guardrails on the Argumentative Strength of LLMs in Hate Speech Countering

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the argumentative strength, cogency, and safety of model-generated counterspeech against race-based hate speech from a White Supremacy Forum dataset, and testing safety mechanisms using explicitly prejudiced prompts and slurs targeting ethnic minorities.

Evaluating model-generated counterspeech in response to xenophobic and anti-immigrant hate speech, and safety testing the model's response to prompts soliciting jokes or offensive replies about migrants.

Evaluating the quality of counterspeech generated against religiously targeted hate speech, and testing safety guardrails by prompting the model to generate offensive replies or jokes targeting specific religious groups (e.g., Muslims, Jews).

Assessing counterspeech generation against gender-based hate speech and evaluating model safety/refusal rates using explicitly offensive prompts targeting women (e.g., requesting jokes using gendered slurs or offensive replies to statements about abortion).

Evaluating counterspeech responses to homophobic hate speech and testing model safety by providing prompts that solicit offensive replies to statements about being gay or requesting jokes using homophobic slurs.
Evaluating model-generated counterspeech against hate speech targeting specific social classes sourced from the White Supremacy Forum dataset.
